key_findings.finding: The ORD database contains an exact product match for coupling Boc-protected N-methyl-4-aminobutyric acid with nitro-phenylenediamine to give the requested aryl amide (reaction ID ord-9961e7a62ca84c3a8fba3cbea619a658).

The matching record lists the acid, nitro-phenylenediamine, DIPEA (Hünig's base), HOBt, sodium bicarbonate, dichloromethane, and 1,2-dichloroethane; these support a standard activated-carboxyl amide coupling under anhydrous chlorinated-solvent conditions, although the database record does not explicitly show a conventional carbodiimide or uronium coupling reagent.

The substrate has two aryl amino groups, so chemoselectivity is intrinsically imperfect; the observed product is consistent with acylation at one aniline nitrogen while retaining the other NH2. Use controlled stoichiometry and mild base, and consider protecting one amino group if regio/chemoselectivity or conversion is inadequate. This selectivity recommendation is an interpretation of the exact reaction structure rather than an explicitly stated database condition.
